stories.title: Australia to evacuate sub-Antarctic research base over bird flu fears
stories.summary: Australia will evacuate all workers from Macquarie Island research station due to the risk of H5N1 bird flu affecting local wildlife and causing psychosocial stress. Thousands of elephant seals on Macquarie Island are vulnerable to H5N1, with many expected to die during the breeding season from September to November. As of August 28, Australia reported 341 H5 bird flu cases but no infections in poultry or agriculture, maintaining low human risk but high concern for animal health and worker wellbeing. Australia said on Aug 28 it would evacuate workers from a research station on a remote island over the “psychosocial” risk caused by a potential outbreak of the highly contagious H5N1 avian influenza. Macquarie Island lies halfway between Tasmania and the Antarctic and is home to an Australian research station as well as thousands of elephant seals. The mammals are highly susceptible to H5N1 bird flu and while no cases have been detected on the island, officials said many were expected to die during the breeding season from September through November. “While the risk to humans of H5 bird flu is considered low, we can’t ignore the psychosocial risks of living near potentially large numbers of affected animals,” said Sean Sullivan, deputy secretary at Canberra’s Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water. “Our expeditioners already live and work in one of the world’s most remote and challenging environments. “It is important that we minimise any additional risks that could affect their wellbeing and the safe operation of our stations.” Macquarie’s 24 tradespeople, scientists and support staff will be evacuated on the RSV Nuyina icebreaker in September or early October, the environment ministry said. Officials in June reported thousands of elephant seal pups had died of bird flu on another remote Australian territory, the Heard and McDonald Islands. The country was for years the only continental landmass free of the H5 strain, which has caused severe disease and death in poultry and wild birds worldwide.

stories.title: (LEAD) N. Korea completes new railway station at Wonsan-Kalma resort
stories.summary: North Korea has finished building a railway station at the Wonsan-Kalma tourist area on the east coast, state media said Friday, as the nation seeks to nurture tourism. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said a ceremony marking the completion of Myongsasimni Railway Station took place the previous day, attended by high-ranking officials, including Vice Premier Pak Hun. State media lauded the 7,000-square-meter station as a "model of Korean-style local railway station," built to serve the needs of tourist travel. The resort, one of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un's signature development projects, officially opened in June 2025 and can reportedly hold up to 20,000 visitors at a time. While visiting the resort in June to inspect its facilities, Kim unveiled plans to modernize railway stations in provincial cities across the country, urging officials to draw on lessons from the project. Kim also flagged "some shortcomings" in the station's construction at that time, according to the KCNA, calling on workers to tighten quality control and upgrade the skills of the construction team. A KCNA photo released showed the station was then called Kalma Tourist Railway Station. Its name appears to have since been changed to Myongsasimni Railway Station, Chang Yoon-jeong, deputy spokesperson at South Korea's unification ministry, said at a regular briefing Friday, citing the absence of any report on a second station and Kim's remarks on the need for further construction work there. The North has ramped up efforts to draw visitors to the resort, running domestic flights to and from Pyongyang since July 23. According to Flightradar24, a flight-tracking site, state carrier Air Koryo operates the route twice a week, on Mondays and Thursdays, using the Ukrainian company Antonov's An-148 aircraft. Pyongyang's state media have launched a promotional campaign for the resort, claiming tens of thousands of people have visited the zone this summer. "The Wonsan-Kalma coastal tourist area in the DPRK is now overflowing with many visitors who came from across the country by train or bus to enjoy the Korean-style tourist culture," the KCNA reported Saturday.

stories.title: From maligned second city to Insta magnet: Marseille isFrance’s new capital of overtourism
stories.summary: This summer has been a tipping point. But it’s not too late to save what makes this place unique When I first started visiting Marseille more than 20 years ago, few could have predicted that France’s then beleaguered second city would become one of the most popular destinations in the most-visited country in the world . Tarnished by stereotypes and home to some of Europe’s most disadvantaged neighbourhoods, the port city seemed down on its luck, unloved and, in the eyes of many, somewhere to avoid. Tourists stopping at the city’s Saint-Charles station would clutch their bags while waiting for their connecting train to rural Provence, or the beaches of the Côte d’Azur. Two decades on, poverty
